climate.overview_html: The headline new item on September 11 is the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season tying—and, by day’s end, likely breaking—the satellite-era record for the latest date of a season’s first hurricane: as of September 11 no Atlantic hurricane has formed, equalling the prior record dates of September 11 set in both 2002 and 2013. The direct cause is the intensifying Super El Niño, which is generating anomalously strong upper-level westerly winds and vertical shear over the tropical Atlantic and suppressing storm development even as the Eastern Pacific has already produced 13 named storms, four hurricanes, and two major hurricanes. The ENSO backdrop remains defined by the WMO SON 2026 Global Seasonal Climate Update (September 8): near-100% probability El Niño persists through DJF 2026/27, Niño 3.4 anomaly at 3.6°C for SON, co-developing positive IOD at ~0.9°C, now confirmed by the NOAA CPC September 2026 ENSO Diagnostic Discussion (“El Niño Advisory”; >90% probability of a very strong event through DJF; 69% probability of a historically unprecedented event with Niño 3.4 ≥+2.5°C for 3-month ONI, exceeding the 1997–98 and 2015–16 records). From the continuing 7-day window: Copernicus August 2026 bulletin (1.65°C, warmest August and hottest boreal summer on record); Carbon Brief September 2026 monthly analysis (2026 tracking second-warmest year; 2027 the likely all-time record as El Niño peaks); the Nepal–Tibet GLOF death toll now at 1,412+ (1,369 Nepal + 43 Tibet) with ~5,651+ still missing — rescue operations ongoing with 5,000+ personnel; and EFFIS European burnt area at approximately 651,267 ha, with the extreme wildfire and drought emergency now transitioning to “flash-flood season” as the Mediterranean severe weather outbreak confirmed active on September 10–11.

items.headline: 2026 Atlantic Hurricane Season Ties Satellite-Era Record for Latest First Hurricane — Five Named Storms, Zero Hurricanes Through September 11; Super El Niño Wind Shear Suppression; NOAA CPC September ENSO Diagnostic Confirms “El Niño Advisory,” >90% Probability Very Strong Event Through DJF
items.summary: As of September 11, 2026, the Atlantic hurricane season has produced five named storms — Arthur (June 17-18), Bertha (July 19-23), Cristobal (August 12-13), Dolly (August 27-28), and Edouard (August 31-September 2) — but not a single hurricane. If no hurricane forms on September 11, the 2026 season will break the satellite-era record (dating to 1966) for the latest first hurricane of a season; the previous record was September 11, set in both 2002 and 2013. The Eastern Pacific has simultaneously produced 13 named storms, four hurricanes, and two major hurricanes — the inverse pattern classic to El Niño seasons. The NOAA Climate Prediction Center September 2026 ENSO Diagnostic Discussion, issued today, maintains the El Niño Advisory, assigns greater than 90% probability to a very strong event persisting through December–February 2026/27, and places 69% probability on a historically unprecedented event in which the 3-month ONI reaches +2.5°C or above, which would exceed the 1997–98 and 2015–16 records. If no Atlantic hurricane forms by November 30, 2026 would become the first hurricane-free Atlantic season in the satellite era.

items.headline: Copernicus August 2026 Climate Bulletin: Warmest August on Record at 1.65°C Above Pre-Industrial — Beats August 2024 by 0.14°C; Completes Hottest Boreal Summer on Record; 2026 Now ~75% Likely to Be Warmest Year in ERA5; SST Hits 21.1°C on August 22 (New August Day Record)
items.summary: The Copernicus Climate Change Service August 2026 climate bulletin confirms August 2026 as the warmest August in the ERA5 dataset at 1.65°C above the pre-industrial baseline — beating August 2024 (1.51°C) by 0.14°C. August 2026 completes the hottest boreal summer (June–August) on record globally. Climatologist Zeke Hausfather notes that with eight months in the record, 2026 carries approximately 75% probability of becoming the warmest calendar year in ERA5. Daily global sea surface temperature on August 22 reached 21.1°C — a new record for any August day. The developing Super El Niño adds further thermodynamic fuel to the ongoing temperature trajectory.

items.headline: Carbon Brief State of the Climate September 2026: Strong El Niño Puts 2026 on Track for Second-Warmest Year; August 2026 First Month Since November 2025 to Individually Exceed 1.5°C; 2027 Most Likely to Set New All-Time Record
items.summary: Carbon Brief's September 2026 monthly state-of-the-climate analysis synthesises the latest surface temperature, sea surface temperature, and ENSO data to conclude that 2026 is on track to be the second warmest year in the instrumental record — with 2027 the likely candidate for a new all-time record as the Super El Niño's atmospheric warming peak is expected to arrive on a 3–6 month lag. August 2026 at 1.65°C was the first individual month since November 2025 to exceed 1.5°C above pre-industrial, marking a renewed and potentially sustained exceedance rather than a brief spike. The article synthesises forecasts from Copernicus C3S, Berkeley Earth, NOAA, and NASA GISS.

items.headline: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse: UPDATED TOLL — 1,412+ Dead (1,369 Nepal + 43 Tibet); ~5,651+ Missing (5,132 Nepal + 519 Tibet); Barrier Lake Risk Ongoing; Rescue Operations Continue
items.summary: The confirmed death toll has risen to at least 1,412 as of September 11: 1,369 in Nepal and 43 in Tibet. The missing-persons count stands at approximately 5,651 (5,132 Nepal, 519 Tibet). The disaster originated on August 27 from a glacier collapse on Langtang Lirung at ~5,200 m, generating a seismic signal of Ms 5.2. Debris has been recovered 240 km downstream inside India. An unstable barrier lake at the Nepal-China border remains a secondary catastrophic flood threat. More than 5,000 Nepalese army and police remain on search operations; approximately 75 foreign nationals, including Americans, remain unaccounted for.

items.source: JRC EFFIS / Euronews / Severe Weather EU
items.headline: EU Wildfire and Drought Emergency Transitions to “Flash-Flood Season”: ~651,267 ha Burned; Mediterranean Severe Weather Outbreak Active September 10–11; Rhine at 1880 Low; Paks Nuclear Curtailed; Pattern Flip Confirmed
items.summary: JRC EFFIS reports a cumulative EU-wide burnt area of approximately 651,267 hectares. Very Extreme Fire Danger continues across Iberia, France, Alps, Balkans, Greece, Turkey, and Ukraine. Rhine water levels remain at their lowest since 1880; the Danube is at record-low stage near Budapest; Hungary's Paks Nuclear Power Plant continues cooling-water curtailment. The violent pattern flip that forecasters warned about — from record summer heat dome to 'flash-flood season' — is now confirmed with the Mediterranean severe weather outbreak active on September 10–11. A deep upper-level trough is generating extreme instability over the charged Mediterranean Sea, producing large-to-giant hail, flooding, and damaging winds from the Balearic Islands through Northern Italy and the Adriatic coast.

items.source: WMO Global Producing Centres / ECMWF / NCEP / JMA
items.headline: WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update SON 2026: El Niño Deepens to 3.6°C Niño 3.4 Anomaly for September–November; Near-100% Probability Persists Through DJF; Positive IOD Co-Developing at 0.9°C; Both Tropical Atlantic Basins Above Normal
items.summary: WMO's September 8 Global Seasonal Climate Update for the SON 2026 season confirms the El Niño is deepening on its projected trajectory. Multi-model ensemble forecasts place the seasonal average Niño 3.4 SST anomaly at approximately 3.6°C for September–November 2026, with the intensification trajectory peaking in November–December. Near-100% probability is assigned to El Niño persisting through both the SON and DJF 2026/27 seasons. A positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) phase is co-developing, with a SON seasonal mean value of approximately 0.9°C, adding a further global teleconnection amplifier. Both the North and South Tropical Atlantic basins are forecast to remain above normal.

weather.overview_html: The dominant development on September 11 is that the HIGH RISK Mediterranean severe weather outbreak forecast yesterday is now active, with flash flooding confirmed across Liguria, northern Italy, and the Adriatic coast; giant hail reported across the northern Mediterranean; and tornado risk persisting over the Croatian coastline through the afternoon — the pattern flip from the record-hot summer heat dome to “flash-flood season” is fully underway. Simultaneously, the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season has tied and is on track to break the satellite-era record for latest first hurricane: as of September 11, five named storms have formed but not a single hurricane. The El Niño-driven wind shear over the tropical Atlantic is suppressing any storm development there while the Super El Niño simultaneously amplifies Eastern Pacific and Western Pacific activity. In Nepal, the death toll from the August 27 Langtang Lirung glacier collapse has climbed to 1,412+ (1,369 Nepal + 43 Tibet) with approximately 5,651 still missing. ASEAN Level 3 haze, Pakistan monsoon flooding, and the Europe wildfire and drought emergency remain active.

items.source: Severe Weather Europe / EUMETSAT / ESTOFEX / Copernicus EMS
items.headline: Mediterranean Severe Weather Outbreak ACTIVE: Flash Flooding Confirmed Liguria and Northern Italy; Giant Hail Adriatic; Tornado Risk Croatian Coast; Record-Charged Mediterranean Fuelling Deep Convection; Pattern Flip to Flash-Flood Season Confirmed
items.summary: The HIGH RISK Mediterranean severe weather outbreak forecast for September 10–11 is now active. Flash flooding has been confirmed in Liguria and northern Italy where extreme instability from the record-warm Mediterranean Sea is combining with strong vertical shear from the incoming trough. Giant hail has been reported across the northern Mediterranean coast. Tornado risk persists over the Croatian Adriatic coastline. A Copernicus Emergency Management Service activation (EMSR843) has been issued for affected Italian regions. The event marks the pattern flip from Europe's record-hot summer heat dome to 'flash-flood season' — the moment Mediterranean forecasters warned about when they identified the exceptionally charged sea-surface temperatures and heat content generated by the record 2026 European heatwave.

items.headline: 2026 Atlantic Hurricane Season Ties Satellite-Era Record: Zero Hurricanes Through September 11 — Fewest Named Storms Since 1966 at This Date; El Niño Wind Shear Suppression; First Hurricane-Free Season Would Be Historic
items.summary: The 2026 Atlantic hurricane season is producing its least active start in at least 60 years of modern records. Five named tropical cyclones (Arthur through Edouard) have formed but none reached hurricane strength, and NHC forecasts no tropical cyclone activity in the Atlantic basin during the next seven days. September 11 ties the satellite-era (1966–present) record for latest first Atlantic hurricane — the same milestone was reached in 2002 and 2013. If no hurricane forms for the remainder of the season, 2026 would be the first hurricane-free Atlantic season in the satellite era. El Niño is responsible: anomalously strong upper-level westerly winds are creating excessive vertical wind shear over the tropical Atlantic, preventing storm organisation. In contrast, the Eastern Pacific has produced 13 named storms, four hurricanes, and two major hurricanes — the standard El Niño inverse basin seesaw pattern.

items.source: Honolulu Civil Beat / CNN / Hawaii HIEMA
items.headline: Hurricane Lowell POST-PASSAGE: Weakened to Tropical Storm; At Least 1 Dead; ~42,000 Without Power on Kaua‘i; Poipu Homes Lifted Off Foundations; Waimea Pier Destroyed; First Tornado Watch in Hawaii History; Hundreds of Millions in Damage
items.summary: Lowell weakened to tropical storm status on September 9, turning northwest away from the Hawaiian Islands, but left a trail of significant destruction. On Kauai's south shore, the storm lifted homes off their foundations and split at least one structure in two. The Sheraton Poipu's oceanfront restaurant was destroyed. North Shore and Westside highways remained impassable due to flooding and debris. A homeless man on Oahu died after a tree fell on his tent during the storm. The Kauai Island Utility Cooperative reported nearly all members without power early Tuesday. Hawaii emergency managers declared it the worst hurricane impact on the islands since Iniki in 1992. The NWS briefly issued the first-ever Tornado Watch for the Hawaiian Islands during Lowell's approach.

items.source: ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre / Channel NewsAsia / Euronews
items.headline: SE Asia Haze: ASEAN Level 3 Transboundary Haze Alert Remains Active (Since August 26); ~300,000 ha Active Fires Kalimantan; Serian (Sarawak) State of Emergency Continuing; 1.4 Million Malaysian Students in Remote Learning; Below-Normal Rainfall Forecast Through October
items.summary: The ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre's Level 3 transboundary haze alert, first issued August 26, remains in force as of September 11. Approximately 300,000 hectares of active fires in Indonesian Kalimantan continue generating dense smoke with PM2.5 concentrations above 500 µg/m³ in parts of Sarawak and Brunei. The emergency declaration in Serian, Sarawak remains active. Malaysia has kept 1.4 million students in remote learning across Sarawak, Sabah, and parts of Peninsular Malaysia. Indonesia's BNPB has deployed 12,000 personnel and water-bombing aircraft across four provinces. IQAir forecasts below-normal rainfall across the southern ASEAN region through October, sustaining elevated fire risk through at least the end of Q3 2026.

items.headline: IMD Heavy-to-Very-Heavy Rainfall Alert for East India September 8–11: Well Marked Low-Pressure Area Over Madhya Pradesh; Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh in Heavy Rain Risk Zone; Monsoon 2026 Season Toll Passes 100
items.summary: India's Meteorological Department issued a heavy-to-very-heavy rainfall alert for East India on September 8, covering Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Jharkhand, and Chhattisgarh for a 3–4 day window, driven by a Well Marked Low-Pressure Area over northeast Madhya Pradesh. India's 2026 monsoon season has now claimed more than 100 lives since July, with Assam hardest hit, followed by Kerala. Widespread flooding in northeastern India between June and August affected more than 500,000 people. The alert period ends September 11 as the system weakens and moves eastward into the Bay of Bengal.

renewables.overview_html: The new September 11 item is from Indian Infrastructure reporting India added 16.39 GW of renewable capacity in April–July 2026 (14.33 GW solar + 2.04 GW wind), placing the country on track for approximately 50 GW of renewable additions in FY 2026–27, with grid-scale battery storage now growing faster than solar and wind on a percentage basis. From the continuing window: Shell Energy Philippines signed a second 15-year PSA with Greenlight Renewables for 120 MWp from Phase 2 of the San Isidro Solar Project in Leyte, bringing total committed capacity to 240 MWp; and Qualitas Energy completed the acquisition of Cero Generation’s 5.8 GW European solar pipeline from Macquarie Asset Management (Spain, Italy, Poland, Greece, Finland). The broader macro context from the IEA’s 2026 energy investment outlook: total renewable power investment is forecast at $665 billion for 2026, with solar alone attracting $365 billion.

items.headline: India Clean Power Uptake: 16.39 GW Renewable Capacity Added April–July 2026 (14.33 GW Solar + 2.04 GW Wind); Storage Additions Accelerating Faster Than Generation; FY26–27 Tracking ~50 GW Annual Total
items.summary: India added 16.39 GW of renewable energy capacity in the April–July 2026 period (the first four months of India's fiscal year 2026–27), comprising 14.33 GW of solar PV and 2.04 GW of wind. Battery energy storage system (BESS) additions are accelerating at a faster percentage pace than either solar or wind, consistent with India's draft Central Electricity Authority regulation requiring co-located storage for all new projects above 50 MW. The April–July run rate places India on track for approximately 50 GW of annual renewable additions in FY 2026–27, which would be a record for the country and continue its trajectory as the third-largest renewable market behind China and the United States.

items.headline: Shell Energy Philippines Signs Second 15-Year PSA With Greenlight Renewables for 120 MWp Phase 2 San Isidro Solar (Leyte) — Total Committed Capacity Now 240 MWp; Phase 2 Online July 2026
items.summary: Shell Energy Philippines signed a second 15-year power supply agreement with Greenlight Renewables, a joint venture between Shell and Emerging Power, Inc. (EPI), for an additional 120 MWp sourced from Phase 2 of the San Isidro Solar Power Project in Leyte. Phase 2 was energised on July 30, 2026. Combined with Phase 1's agreement, Shell Energy's total committed capacity from the San Isidro project reaches 240 MWp — supplying approximately 100 commercial and industrial customers across the Philippines. The deal strengthens Shell's retail renewables position in one of Asia's fastest-growing power markets.

items.headline: Qualitas Energy Acquires Cero Generation’s Core European Platform From Macquarie Asset Management — 5.8 GW Solar Pipeline Across Spain, Italy, Poland, Greece, Finland; Cero’s Nordic Operations Retained by Macquarie
items.summary: Madrid-based Qualitas Energy has completed the acquisition of Cero Generation's core European solar development platform from Macquarie Asset Management, gaining a 5.8 GW pipeline across Spain, Italy, Poland, Greece, and Finland. Macquarie is retaining Cero's Nordic operations. Qualitas Energy becomes one of Southern Europe's largest independent solar developers with this transaction. The deal reflects continued institutional capital appetite for early-to-mid stage development platforms in EU markets with strong capacity auction visibility under REPowerEU.

items.headline: IEA 2026 Energy Investment Outlook: $665 Billion in Global Renewable Power Investment Forecast; Solar Alone $365 Billion; U.S. Solar Capacity Additions Up 45% YoY in Q2 2026 (11.4 GWdc); Batteries Emerging as Grid-Critical Infrastructure
items.summary: The IEA's 2026 energy investment outlook projects total renewable power investment globally at approximately $665 billion for 2026, with solar PV alone attracting roughly $365 billion — the single largest destination for generation capital. The U.S. solar industry added 11.4 GWdc of new capacity in Q2 2026, a 45% year-over-year increase and a 43% increase from Q1, driven by utility-scale projects and the continued buildout of co-located storage. Battery energy storage systems are increasingly characterised as critical grid infrastructure in markets with high solar penetration: California, Germany, South Australia, Texas, and the UK have all seen strong utility-scale battery growth in 2026.

items.headline: Google, MN8 Energy, and Eos Energy Sign Round-the-Clock PPA: 86 MW Solar + 70 MW/280 MWh Lithium-Ion + 10 MW/100 MWh Zinc Long-Duration Storage on Reclaimed West Virginia Coal Mine; Powers Google’s PJM-Region Data Centres From 2028
items.summary: MN8 Energy, Eos Energy Enterprises, and Google announced a collaboration to deliver clean, around-the-clock power to the PJM grid from a reclaimed coal mine site in West Virginia. The project pairs 86 MW of utility-scale solar with 70 MW/280 MWh of conventional lithium-ion storage (operational 2029) and 10 MW/100 MWh of Eos's proprietary Z3™ zinc-based long-duration energy storage (operational 2030). Google will purchase energy, capacity, and clean energy attributes under a long-term PPA to support its West Virginia data centre. The deal represents one of the first commercial-scale deployments of grid-connected zinc LDES alongside lithium-ion in a US renewable project.

science.overview_html: The science window continues to be defined by last week’s dense cluster of AI weather research. WeatherNext 3 (Google DeepMind, arXiv:2609.03582) remains the headline result: the first global AI model to ingest live geostationary satellite data and raw station observations, delivering new hourly forecasts at 0.1° / 11-km resolution with state-of-the-art probabilistic skill across the 10-day medium range, deployed in Google Search, Gemini, and Maps. arXiv:2609.08241 (EastAsiaClimateExtremes) is the newest paper in the window, delivering an AI-ready benchmark for East Asian atmospheric and marine extreme events co-registered with ECMWF S2S hindcasts — filling a critical gap for subseasonal prediction research. Supporting papers in the window include CloudCast v2 extending ML cloud-cover forecasting to 12-hour lead times — directly relevant to solar irradiance dispatch, the MeteoSwiss hail nowcasting study showing dual-pol radar and lightning improve skill beyond architecture changes alone, KMA’s TC downscaling work demonstrating a critical 20–50-km resolution threshold for subseasonal cyclone genesis fidelity, and ECMWF AI Weather Quest’s first-year conclusion with 42 teams, where the winning submission beat ECMWF’s own S2S ensemble. The September 10–11 Mediterranean outbreak is a live test of ML extreme weather skill.

items.source: arXiv / Fudan University / ECMWF / Chinese Academy of Sciences
items.headline: arXiv 2609.08241 (EastAsiaClimateExtremes): First AI-Ready Weekly Benchmark Dataset for East Asian Atmospheric and Oceanic Extremes — AHT, Heavy Rainfall, Marine Heatwaves; Co-Registered With ECMWF S2S Hindcasts; Open on GitHub
items.summary: EastAsiaClimateExtremes is an open benchmark dataset providing ERA5/OISST reanalysis-based weekly extreme labels and event metrics for three categories — anomalously high temperature (AHT), heavy rainfall (HR), and marine heatwaves (MHW) — over East Asia. The dataset is co-registered with ECMWF S2S hindcast outputs on a common spatial grid and temporal framework, enabling direct comparison between reanalysis-derived ground-truth labels and dynamical model sub-seasonal forecasts. The paper addresses a gap in AI-based climate extreme prediction: despite growing interest, event-based AI-ready datasets for East Asia remain sparse, constraining efforts to benchmark and improve AI models at subseasonal timescales where dynamical models face their largest skill gaps.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03582 (WeatherNext 3): Google DeepMind’s Hourly 0.1° Global AI Weather Model Achieves New State-of-the-Art Probabilistic Skill by Ingesting Live Geostationary Satellite Data — Deployed in Google Search, Gemini, Maps
items.meta: Google DeepMind & Google Research · arXiv:2609.03582 · September 3, 2026 · Deployed in Google Search, Gemini, Maps, BigQuery, Earth Engine
items.summary: WeatherNext 3 is the first major global AI model to ingest live geostationary satellite data directly and train on raw weather station observations — eliminating the 6-to-7-hour data lag of NWP-based ERA5 initial conditions. It generates new forecasts every hour at 0.1° (~11 km) spatial resolution, placing its resolution on par with ECMWF HRES. On both probabilistic (CRPS) and deterministic skill score benchmarks across the full 10-day medium range, WeatherNext 3 establishes a new state-of-the-art for probabilistic global AI weather forecasting. The model is deployed in production inside Google Search, Gemini, Google Maps, BigQuery, and Earth Engine.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03763 (CloudCast v2): AI Cloud Cover Forecasting Extended From 1–3 h to 12 h Lead Time at 4-km / 15-Minute Resolution, Trained on Copernicus CERRA Reanalysis — Competitive With NWP to 8 h; Direct Input to Solar Dispatch
items.meta: Nielsen, Bjørk, Dittmer et al. (DTU / DMI) · arXiv:2609.03763 · September 3, 2026
items.summary: CloudCast v2 extends the original CloudCast nowcasting system to 12-hour lead times at 15-minute temporal resolution and 4-km spatial resolution. The model is trained on the Copernicus European Regional Reanalysis (CERRA) and evaluated against HARMONIE-AROME NWP model output. CloudCast v2 achieves skill competitive with numerical weather prediction to approximately 8-hour lead times on continuous cloud fraction, and substantially outperforms NWP at 1–4 hours on rapid cloud evolution metrics. Cloud cover is the primary driver of solar irradiance forecast error at sub-day timescales, making 12-hour ML cloud forecasting a direct input to solar energy dispatch and grid balancing systems.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.04427: Input Data Sensitivity in Deep-Learning Hail Nowcasting — More Training Data Beats Architecture Changes; Dual-Pol Radar and Lightning Improve Skill; Radar Reflectivity Alone Insufficient for Large-Hail Discrimination
items.meta: Pacey, Miralles, Hamann, Martius (Univ. Bern / MeteoSwiss) · arXiv:2609.04427 · September 3, 2026
items.summary: This paper systematically evaluates how input data choices affect deep-learning hail nowcasting skill without changing model architecture. Adding dual-polarisation radar variables (ZDR, KDP, ρhv) and lightning stroke-density layers each improve skill more than architectural changes alone. Radar reflectivity alone is insufficient for discriminating large-hail (≥2 cm) from ordinary convective precipitation at short lead times. The study uses a Swiss dataset of 6 hail seasons and evaluates on a spatially separated test domain. Directly relevant to the September 10–11 Mediterranean outbreak, where hail up to 10 cm was forecast.

items.headline: ECMWF AI Weather Quest: First Year Concludes — 42 Teams From 30+ Countries; DJF 2025/26 Hindcast Challenge Winner Beats ECMWF S2S Ensemble; Annual Awards September 24
items.meta: ECMWF Science Blog · September 2026 · Competition phase: August 2025–September 2026 · Annual awards: 24 Sep 2026
items.summary: ECMWF's AI Weather Quest — an international competition for AI/ML sub-seasonal forecasting from August 2025 to September 2026 — is concluding its first year, with an awards ceremony scheduled for September 24, 2026. 42 teams from 30+ countries participated, submitting weekly AI-based forecasts for 2-week ensemble temperature and precipitation anomalies globally. The winning DJF 2025/26 hindcast submission outperformed ECMWF's own operational S2S ensemble on the primary skill metric. ECMWF plans to expand the Quest to a second year with longer forecast horizons and a marine heat wave prediction track.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03364: Added Value of Dynamical Downscaling in Sub-Seasonal Tropical Cyclone Forecasting Over the Western North Pacific — GloSea6 Ensemble Experiments Confirm 20–50 km Resolution Threshold for TC Genesis Fidelity
items.meta: Kim et al. (Korea Meteorological Administration) · arXiv:2609.03364 · September 3, 2026
items.summary: This study evaluates tropical cyclone representation in sub-seasonal forecasts using GloSea6 over the western North Pacific. Experiments find a critical resolution threshold near 20–50 km below which TC genesis frequency and track distributions diverge sharply from climatology. Dynamical downscaling of 100 km forecasts to 25 km with a regional model substantially improves TC genesis fidelity, track probability distributions, and intensity statistics at 2–4 week lead times — supporting operational ensemble downscaling as a bridge between global sub-seasonal models and regional TC guidance.

items.title: Perry Weather Raises $110 Million Growth Investment From Silversmith Capital Partners — Hyperlocal Weather Safety Platform Now Covers 3,000+ Organizations (Schools, Construction, Sports Leagues); Plans 50+ New Dallas Hires; Total Funding $131 Million
items.body_html: Perry Weather, the Dallas-based hyperlocal weather safety and operations platform, closed a $110 million growth investment on September 9, led by Silversmith Capital Partners (Boston growth equity), with participation from prior investor Arthur Ventures. The round brings total funding to $131.35 million. Perry Weather pairs purpose-built on-site hardware weather stations with cloud-connected software to deliver real-time hyperlocal monitoring, automated alerts, and AI-assisted siren activation covering lightning, extreme heat, high wind, air quality, and other hazardous conditions. More than 3,000 organizations rely on the platform — school districts, municipal governments, construction firms, manufacturers, and major professional sports leagues. The company plans to add more than 50 new roles through 2027 across software engineering, hardware, product, and support at its Dallas headquarters. The investment will accelerate AI-powered capability development across Perry Weather’s product suite and support geographic expansion into new enterprise market segments. The raise is the largest growth investment in a standalone weather safety startup in 2026 and reflects the convergence of hyperlocal sensor networks, AI, and escalating demand for operational weather risk management driven by more frequent and severe weather events.
items.source_html: Yahoo Finance / Dallas Innovates

items.title: ARC Ride (Kenya) Closes $33.3 Million Series A to Scale Battery-Swapping Electric Motorcycle Network Across Sub-Saharan Africa — IFC, BII, Proparco, Novastar Ventures Lead; 5,000 New E-Motos; Expanding to Ghana, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda
items.body_html: Kenyan electric mobility startup ARC Ride closed a $33.3 million financing round on September 8, comprising a $23 million Series A equity round co-led by Novastar Ventures and Norrsken22, alongside a $10 million debt tranche. Strategic investors include the International Finance Corporation (IFC), British International Investment (BII), Proparco, Musashi Seimitsu, and Talanton. ARC Ride operates a Battery-as-a-Service model in which riders exchange depleted batteries at swap stations rather than owning them, reducing the upfront cost barrier to switching from petrol-powered motorcycles. The company plans to add 5,000 electric motorcycles to its fleet and expand from Kenya into Ghana, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda. Africa's two- and three-wheeler market is one of the highest-emission transportation segments per passenger-kilometer, and battery swapping addresses the range anxiety and grid-charging infrastructure gaps that have constrained EV adoption across the continent.
items.source_html: TechCabal / Launch Base Africa

items.title: Howden Re Launches International Alternative Solutions Practice — Dedicated Parametric, ILS, and Climate-Risk Transfer Team; Hire of 12-Person Ex-Aon Reinsurance Team; Focus on Sovereign Nat-Cat, Food Security, and Transition Risk
items.body_html: Howden Re announced the formal launch of its International Alternative Solutions Practice on September 6, a dedicated team focused on parametric reinsurance, Insurance-Linked Securities (ILS), and bespoke climate-risk transfer structures. The practice is anchored by a 12-person team predominantly hired from Aon’s reinsurance solutions division. Priority markets include sovereign parametric nat-cat covers for Small Island Developing States and lower-middle-income countries, multi-year food security triggers linked to ENSO indices, and transition-risk liability covers for energy companies managing coal asset retirement. The launch reflects continued growth in demand for ILS-style risk transfer as traditional reinsurance capacity tightens on climate-exposed lines.
items.source_html: Howden Re / Reinsurance News

items.title: Nexeon (UK) Closes £100 Million Series D for Silicon Anode Battery Materials — National Wealth Fund and Honda Xcelerator Lead; Expands Teesside Pilot Facility Targeting 10,000-Cycle EV Battery Longevity
items.body_html: Abingdon-based Nexeon closed a £100 million Series D round on September 6, led by the UK’s National Wealth Fund (through UKIB) and Honda Xcelerator Ventures, with Korea Development Bank as strategic co-investor. Nexeon’s silicon anode technology replaces or supplements graphite in EV battery anodes, increasing energy density by up to 20% and targeting cycle lives exceeding 10,000 full charge-discharge cycles — critical for next-generation battery-electric commercial vehicles and long-duration residential storage. Funds will expand Nexeon’s Teesside pilot facility and accelerate scale-up toward a gigawatt-hour-scale manufacturing line. Honda’s participation follows a multi-year joint development agreement.

items.title: Swiss Re: Data Centers and AI Workloads Create $200 Billion Premium Opportunity for Insurers Through 2030 — Hyperscaler Power Demand to Triple; New Nat-Cat Exposure; Cyber-Physical Risk Convergence Identified as Major Coverage Gap
items.body_html: Swiss Re Institute’s September 2026 sigma report quantifies data centres and AI compute infrastructure as a $200 billion cumulative premium opportunity for the global (re)insurance industry through 2030. The report projects that hyperscaler power demand will triple by 2030, creating new concentrations of physical risk exposure — fire, flood, power-interruption, and cooling failure — at a scale that substantially exceeds existing commercial insurance penetration. Swiss Re identifies cyber-physical risk convergence as the major emerging coverage gap: as AI workloads become operationally critical, a single data centre outage can trigger simultaneous property damage, business interruption, and downstream liability claims across multiple policyholders. Nat-cat exposure is also flagged: many hyperscaler campuses in historically low-risk corridors (Iowa, Virginia, Texas) are in locations with rapidly changing flood, heat, and severe-thunderstorm risk profiles. Swiss Re recommends parametric trigger structures and real-time physical risk monitoring as components of a new data-centre risk transfer framework.
items.source_html: Swiss Re Institute / Reuters

items.title: Light (PoweredbyLight) Raises $46 Million Series A Led by Matrix Partners to Scale “Embedded Electricity” Platform — Enables Any Company to Offer Branded Retail Electricity With Built-In VPP Participation; Covers 30% of U.S. Residential Solar Sales
items.body_html: Light (brand: PoweredbyLight), an Austin-based platform that lets any company become a regulated retail electricity provider via API — including licensing, wholesale procurement, billing, customer support, and virtual power plant (VPP) participation — closed a $46 million Series A round led by Matrix Partners with participation from Activate Capital, Spark Capital, Mischief, Gigascale Capital, MCJ, and BoxGroup. Total funding now exceeds $60 million; capital base (equity + credit facility) exceeds $100 million. The partner network covers more than 30% of all U.S. residential solar sales and 500,000+ homeowners. In H1 2026, 100% of new electricity brands entering the Texas ERCOT market launched on Light’s platform. The round positions distributed solar and storage assets as addressable VPP capacity within a mainstream B2B SaaS model.
items.source_html: PR Newswire / Tech Startups
